metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Digital Medication Management domain, covering in-home dispensing, remote care, pharmacy supply, and deployment/fleet operations.
metadata.flowModelNote: Flows describe outcome journeys across bricks; steps carry key facts, pain points, and brick dependencies.

rootGroups.name: In-Home Dispensing Journeys
rootGroups.description: The core in-home journeys: dispensing and confirming a scheduled dose, and detecting and escalating a missed one.

streams.name: Dispense and Confirm a Scheduled Dose
streams.description: The end-to-end journey by which a patient is reminded of a due dose, confirms it, and the device releases exactly the correct pouch — the core value the whole service exists to deliver.
outcomes: Fewer routine home visits for pill handling

flows.title: Scheduled dose from reminder to confirmed release
flows.description: From the scheduled time to a confirmed, recorded dose.

steps.title: Reach the scheduled occasion
keyFacts: The active schedule defines exactly which medicines are due at this occasion.
The device must act reliably even if briefly offline.
painPoints: A stale schedule after a prescription change could prompt the wrong dose.
Clock or timezone drift on the device would mis-time reminders.

dependencies.name: Medication Schedule and Regimen Management
dependencies.description: Medication Schedule and Regimen Management brick.
dependencies.how: Provides the active occasion plan that drives the reminder.

dependencies.name: Device Firmware and On-Device Runtime
dependencies.description: Device Firmware and On-Device Runtime brick.
dependencies.how: Runs the real-time on-device scheduling and I/O.

steps.title: Prompt the patient unmistakably
keyFacts: Sound, light, on-screen text, and voice make the due dose clear to frail users.
Prompt intensity escalates if the patient does not respond.
painPoints: Prompts that are too subtle are missed; too aggressive erodes trust.
Sensory or language mismatch leaves the patient unsure what to do.

dependencies.name: Patient Reminder and Confirmation Experience
dependencies.description: Patient Reminder and Confirmation Experience brick.
dependencies.how: Presents the multi-sensory reminder and confirmation control.

steps.title: Confirm and release the correct pouch
keyFacts: On confirmation the device verifies and pre-cuts exactly the due pouch.
The dispense outcome is recorded as the source of adherence truth.
painPoints: A mechanism jam must fail safe, never release the wrong pouch.
A missed confirmation must flow to the safety net, not be dropped.

dependencies.name: Dose Dispensing Engine and Mechanism
dependencies.description: Dose Dispensing Engine and Mechanism brick.
dependencies.how: Verifies the pouch and drives the cut-and-release mechanism.

dependencies.name: Device Connectivity and Telemetry
dependencies.description: Device Connectivity and Telemetry brick.
dependencies.how: Streams the dose event to the cloud.

dependencies.name: Adherence Tracking and Dose Ledger
dependencies.description: Adherence Tracking and Dose Ledger brick.
dependencies.how: Records the confirmed dose in the adherence ledger.

streams.name: Detect and Escalate a Missed Dose Safely
streams.description: The safety-net journey that turns an unconfirmed or missed dose into a secured dose and a prioritized alarm routed to the right carer, tracked to safe resolution.

flows.title: From unconfirmed dose to resolved alarm
flows.description: Detect a missed dose, secure it, alarm the right carer, and resolve it.

steps.title: Detect the miss and secure the dose
keyFacts: After repeated reminders an untaken dose is locked back inside the cabinet.
Detection uses adherence context to judge severity.
painPoints: False positives cause alarm fatigue; misses undermine safety.
An unsecured dose left accessible is a clinical risk.

dependencies.name: Patient Reminder and Confirmation Experience

dependencies.description: Missed-Dose Alarm and Escalation Engine brick.

steps.title: Route the alarm to the right carer
keyFacts: Routing rules resolve the on-duty or on-call carer by client, shift, and severity.
Alarms carry enough context to act without a visit.
painPoints: Wrong routing delays response; noisy alarms get ignored.
Out-of-hours gaps leave alarms unworked.

steps.title: Resolve remotely or escalate, and record
keyFacts: Carers act remotely first: message, video-coach, or assisted-release.
The resolution is recorded for accountability.
painPoints: If remote action fails, escalation to a visit must be timely.
An unrecorded resolution breaks the audit trail.

rootGroups.name: Remote Care Journeys
rootGroups.description: How care staff supervise caseloads remotely and assist difficult doses by video.

streams.name: Monitor a Caseload and Act Remotely
streams.description: The nurse's journey of supervising a whole caseload from the portal — seeing who is safe, who needs attention, and acting remotely — so physical visits go only where they change an outcome.

flows.title: A monitored morning round
flows.description: Triage the caseload, work exceptions, and act where needed.

steps.title: Scan the whole caseload
keyFacts: One view shows adherence, open alarms, and device status across clients.
Clients needing attention are prioritized to the top.
painPoints: A cluttered view hides genuine need.
Distrust in the data forces redundant physical checks.

steps.title: Work the exceptions
keyFacts: Open alarms and adverse trends are worked from the portal.
Schedules and history are visible per client for context.
painPoints: Without context, nurses over-escalate to visits.
Switching tools mid-triage loses time.

Manual documentation erodes reclaimed time.

streams.name: Assist a Difficult Dose by Video
streams.description: The assisted-medication journey where a carer connects to a patient's device to coach a difficult or high-risk dose and, in assisted mode, authorize a supervised release — extending the service to higher-acuity patients.
outcomes: More high-acuity patients kept at home
Fewer avoidable visits for complex doses

flows.title: Assisted medication over video
flows.description: Establish an authorized session, coach the dose, and record it.

steps.title: Establish an authorized session
keyFacts: Only staff with rights to the patient may open a session.
Patient consent is checked before connecting.
painPoints: An unauthorized or non-consented session is a serious breach.
Poor connectivity disrupts a time-sensitive dose.

steps.title: Coach the patient through the dose
keyFacts: The carer guides the patient by two-way video and messaging.
In assisted mode the carer can authorize a supervised release.
painPoints: Miscommunication risks a wrong or skipped dose.
Assisted release must be tightly controlled.

rootGroups.name: Pharmacy Supply Journeys
rootGroups.description: The pouch-supply and prescription-alignment journeys that keep devices accurately stocked.

streams.name: Fill and Load an Accurate Pouch Roll
streams.description: The pharmacy supply journey from a device-linked dose-packaging order to a correctly packed, device-compatible roll delivered and confirmed loaded before the device runs empty.

flows.title: Order to loaded roll
flows.description: Generate the order, pack the roll, deliver, and confirm loading.

steps.title: Generate a device-linked order
keyFacts: Orders are built from the active schedule and tied to patient and device.
Replenishment timing is driven by device stock signals.
painPoints: An order built from a stale schedule mismatches the prescription.
Late orders risk a device running empty.

dependencies.name: Medication Schedule and Regimen Management
dependencies.description: Medication Schedule and Regimen Management brick.
dependencies.how: Provides the schedule the order is built from.

dependencies.name: Dose-Packaging Order Management

dependencies.name: Device Replenishment and Stock Signals
dependencies.description: Device Replenishment and Stock Signals brick.

steps.title: Pack and format the roll for the device
keyFacts: Each occasion's medicines are packed and sequenced for reliable dispensing.
Formatting is validated for device compatibility.
painPoints: Incorrect sequencing jams or misfeeds the device.
A packing error propagates to every dose on the roll.

dependencies.name: Pouch Roll Fulfillment and Loading
dependencies.description: Pouch Roll Fulfillment and Loading brick.

steps.title: Deliver, load, and confirm
keyFacts: The roll is delivered and loaded before the device runs low.
Loading is confirmed so supply and dispensing stay in sync.
painPoints: An unconfirmed load leaves stock state wrong.
A late delivery interrupts dosing.

streams.name: Keep Orders Aligned with Prescriptions
streams.description: The interoperability journey that keeps schedules and pouch orders synchronized with current prescriptions, handling mid-cycle changes safely and evidencing compliance to care systems.
outcomes: Interoperable with care and prescription systems

flows.title: Prescription-synced medication management
flows.description: Sync prescriptions, propagate changes safely, and reconcile.

steps.title: Sync current prescription data
keyFacts: Prescriptions are normalized from national and pharmacy sources.
The canonical schedule is derived from current prescriptions.
painPoints: A missed prescription change dispenses the wrong medicine.
Source outages must not silently freeze updates.

steps.title: Propagate a change safely mid-cycle
keyFacts: A change stages a safeguarded schedule update and flags affected rolls.
In-progress rolls are reworked rather than dispensed wrongly.
painPoints: An unsafe mid-cycle change is a direct clinical risk.
Rework that lags leaves a mismatched roll in the device.

rootGroups.name: Deployment and Fleet Journeys
rootGroups.description: Onboarding patients and operating a reliable device fleet at scale.

streams.name: Onboard a Patient onto the Service
streams.description: The deployment journey of bringing a new patient onto the service — assessment, device provisioning, schedule setup, first roll, and first confirmed dose — repeatable at population scale.

flows.title: From assessment to first confirmed dose

steps.title: Assess the client and capture consent
keyFacts: Suitability is assessed and consent captured before provisioning.
The patient profile is created as system of record.
painPoints: Onboarding an unsuitable client risks safety and churn.
Missing consent blocks lawful data handling.

streams.name: Operate a Reliable Device Fleet
streams.description: The operations journey of keeping the whole device fleet healthy, connected, updated, and serviced so that remote monitoring data can be trusted and the service stays available and compliant.

flows.title: Keeping the fleet healthy
flows.description: Monitor health, roll out updates safely, and service devices.

steps.title: Monitor device health across the fleet
keyFacts: Health telemetry from every device feeds the fleet console.
Reliability metrics underpin trust in monitoring.
painPoints: Blind spots let failing devices masquerade as healthy.
Telemetry gaps corrupt adherence signals.
